Batala Bermo is a not-for-profit organisation and all proceeds of the band go toward providing instruments and costumes for the members. Joining Batala is open to everyone, regardless of race, religion, income, sexual orientation or musical experience. Bermo is the local name for Barmouth (our home town) and is part of the wider group of Batala which has its origins in Brazil. The music of Batala originates in Salvador de Bahia in North Eastern Brazil. Batala was formed as the European wing of Cortego Afro, (a style of Brazilian Samba) by Giba Goncalves in Paris in 1997. The music has its roots in African traditional music which found its way to Brazil and has been incorporated in to Brazilian culture since.

The aim of Mach Fringe, based in the town of Machynlleth, Powys, is to foster, encourage and enable arts events, music events, gatherings and procedures that will unite and encourage community activity and cohesion, giving full regard to and including all languages and diversity. Machfringe has been in existence since the early 1990's and has raised thousands of pounds for many charities and put on hundreds of events. It came into existence to provide an alternative to the well respected and excellent classical festival at MOMA - Y Tabernacle arts centre that takes place every August.

The Knighton Festival of Books, Art and Music was established initially in 2018. Its programme includes poetry readings, authors’ talks, concerts, a film, an art and book fair, craft and writing workshops, alongside organised rambles, a town walk and a cycle ride.

Newtown Outdoor Festival is a not-for-profit limited company which is held annually at the beginning of June in the town of Newtown, Powys. It has activities such as guided town walks, historic house tours, navigation, canoeing and guided cycle rides amongst other activities.
